summary: Phase 7 of plan v3 (plans/03_direct-route-forest.md): landed and committed two sorry-free, axiom-clean lemmas toward boxI_lift in Cslib/Logics/Modal/Metalogic/Constructive/Labelled/Soundness.lean -- `ht_le_of_reflTransGen` (rank non-decreasing along forward G.R-reachability, a direct consequence of the graded-rank conjunct) and `raise_subtree` (the recommended downward-cascade helper: raise a node already fixed to a target together with the forward-reachable closure through a chosen Finset of direct raw-neighbours, via repeated cs5FCIncest_lift/F1, well-founded on Set.ncard {q in G.X | ht q >= ht p}; disjointness of sibling closures derived from a last-edge unique-parent argument, no general cycle-freeness lemma needed). `boxI_lift` itself (the ancestor-walk assembly on top of raise_subtree) was drafted but found unsound in its recursive step via live lean_goal checking BEFORE further code was written -- the naive induction hypothesis at each ancestor covers all of G's edges unconditionally, which would let it silently re-derive the already-descended child branch's value, conflicting with that branch's pinned target. This is an engineering induction-hypothesis-shape defect, not a mathematical wall: the fix (a Finset exclusion parameter mirroring raise_subtree's own mechanism, inverted) is fully specified in the plan's Phase 7 partial-progress note and the handoff markdown, but was not implemented within this dispatch's budget. The unsound draft was discarded (never committed, no sorry ever written).

blockers.verbatim_goal: State boxI_lift with the audit §3 signature (schematically): cs5FCIncest r → (v upward-closed) → (botForces upward-closed) → IsDerivationForest G → (∀ a b, G.R a b → r (ρ a) (ρ b)) → ρ x ≤ w' → ∃ ρ', ρ' x = w' ∧ (∀ z, ρ z ≤ ρ' z) ∧ (∀ a b, G.R a b → r (ρ' a) (ρ' b)) ∧ (∀ {φ z}, CKForces r v botForces (ρ z) φ → CKForces r v botForces (ρ' z) φ).
blockers.what_was_tried: Ancestor walk up the unique-parent chain via cs5FCIncest_raise (F2), invoking raise_subtree for sibling branches, with the outer strong-induction-on-ht-x hypothesis applied unconditionally at each ancestor.
blockers.why_it_failed: The induction hypothesis's conclusion covers all of G's edges unconditionally, so applying it to the parent would let it silently re-derive the child branch's value independently via its own internal raise_subtree call, conflicting with that branch's already-pinned target -- fixed by adding a Finset exclusion parameter (exact corrected statement recorded in plans/03_direct-route-forest.md Phase 7 partial-progress note).
